sentences.en: Since the early morning hours, Russian troops are attacking Budapest and our population.
sentences.zh: 从清晨开始，苏联军队一直在进攻布达佩斯和我们的民众。

sentences.en: Please tell the world of the treacherous attack against our struggle for liberty.
sentences.zh: 请向世界讲述我们为争取自由而进行斗争所遭受的奸险攻击。

sentences.en: Our troops are already engaged in fighting.
sentences.zh: 我们的军队已经投入战斗。

sentences.en: Help, help, help.
sentences.zh: 救命，救命，救命。

sentences.en: SOS, SOS, SOS.
sentences.zh: 求救，求救，求救。

sentences.en: The people have just overturned a tram to use as a barricade near this building.
sentences.zh: 人们刚刚推翻了一辆有轨电车，用作这座建筑附近的街垒。

sentences.en: In the building, young people are making Molotov cocktails and hand grenades to fight tanks.
sentences.zh: 在大楼里，年轻人正在制作莫洛托夫鸡尾酒（燃烧瓶）和手榴弹来对抗坦克。

sentences.en: We are quiet, not afraid.
sentences.zh: 我们很镇定，并不害怕。

sentences.en: Send the news to the public of the world and say it should condemn the aggression.
sentences.zh: 把消息发给世界公众，并说它应该谴责这种侵略。

sentences.en: The fighting is very close now.
sentences.zh: 战斗现在非常近了。

sentences.en: And we haven't enough guns in the building.
sentences.zh: 而且我们在大楼里没有足够的枪支。

sentences.en: I don't know how long we can resiSt. Heavy shells are exploding nearby.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我们还能坚持多久。沉重的炮弹在附近爆炸。

sentences.en: Above, jet planes are roaring.
sentences.zh: 头顶上，喷气式飞机在轰鸣。

sentences.en: A shell just exploded nearby.
sentences.zh: 一颗炮弹刚刚在附近爆炸。

sentences.en: Now there is heavy fighting in the direction of the National Theatre, near us in the centre of the city.
sentences.zh: 现在，在靠近我们市中心的国家剧院方向正发生激烈的战斗。

sentences.en: In our building, we have youngsters of 15, men of 40.
sentences.zh: 在我们的楼里，有 15 岁的少年，也有 40 岁的壮年。

sentences.en: Don't worry about us.
sentences.zh: 不要为我们担心。

sentences.en: We are strong, even if we are a small nation.
sentences.zh: 我们很坚强，即使我们是一个小国。

sentences.en: When the fighting is over, we will rebuild our unhappy country.
sentences.zh: 当战斗结束时，我们将重建我们不幸的国家。

sentences.en: So those were telex messages sent from the Hungarian newspaper Sobodnape, which of course, as all of us who speak Hungarian know, translates as a free people.
sentences.zh: 这些是匈牙利报纸《自由人民报》（Sobodnape）发出的电传信息，当然，正如我们所有懂匈牙利语的人所知，它翻译过来就是“自由的人民”。

sentences.en: And it was sent to the Associated Press newsroom in Vienna on the morning of Sunday, the 4th of November, 1956.
sentences.zh: 它是于 1956 年 11 月 4 日星期天早晨发给美联社驻维也纳新闻部的。

sentences.en: And then just before 11am, the line went dead.
sentences.zh: 然后就在上午 11 点之前，线路中断了。

sentences.en: And the newsroom in Vienna heard nothing more.
sentences.zh: 维也纳的新闻部再也没有听到任何消息。

sentences.en: And Dominic, just one of the many tragic scenes from the denouement of the
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，这只是……结局中众多悲惨场景之一……

sentences.en: Hungarian revolution, which is a milestone in the Cold War, of course, a turning point in the history of communism.
sentences.zh: 匈牙利革命，当然，这是冷战的一个里程碑，也是共产主义历史上的一个转折点。

sentences.en: Although, I mean, how much of a turning point is interesting to debate.
sentences.zh: 尽管我的意思是，这究竟算不算是一个转折点，很值得讨论。

sentences.en: And we will explore these issues in today's episode.
sentences.zh: 我们将在今天的节目中探讨这些问题。

sentences.en: But first, could we have a reminder of what's going on?
sentences.zh: 但首先，能给我们回顾一下当前的情况吗？

sentences.en: Because people will remember that our previous episode was dominated by the charismatic
sentences.zh: 因为人们会记得，我们上一集的焦点是富有个人魅力、

sentences.en: swashbuckling, the great blaze of charisma that was Imre Nodge.
sentences.zh: 潇洒不羁、充满领袖魅力的伟大人物——伊姆雷·纳吉。

sentences.en: And I looked up and I discovered it actually means Mr. Big.
sentences.zh: 我查了一下，发现它实际上是“大人物”（Mr. Big）的意思。

sentences.en: So like in Sex and the City.
sentences.zh: 就像《欲望都市》里那样。

sentences.en: Or indeed, live and let die.
sentences.zh: 或者确实，像《生死关头》。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, that reflects our different perspectives, doesn't it, Dominic?
sentences.zh: 是啊，这反映了我们不同的视角，对吧，多米尼克？

sentences.en: It does indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Also, I'll tell you who else it reminds me of is Yorg, which is the name that Andrew Ridgely called
sentences.zh: 另外，我告诉你它还让我想起了谁，那就是 Yorg，这是安德鲁·Ridgeley 对

sentences.en: George Michael.
sentences.zh: 乔治·迈克尔的称呼。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, because it was Yorgios.
sentences.zh: 对，因为那是 Yorgios。

sentences.en: Yorg.
sentences.zh: 约格。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Anyway, that's by the by.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，那是题外话。

sentences.en: Remind us who Nodge is, why he's such a hero, or is he?
sentences.zh: 提醒一下我们纳吉是谁，为什么他是这样一个英雄，或者他是吗？

sentences.en: And what's going on?
sentences.zh: 现在情况怎么样？

sentences.en: All right, we'll come to Nodge in just a sec, just the big context.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们马上就会谈到纳吉，先讲讲宏观背景。

sentences.en: So last time we entered, didn't we, on the 25th of October, 1956, and that was three days into this popular uprising against
sentences.zh: 所以上一次我们切入的时间点，对吧，是 1956 年 10 月 25 日，那是这场反对

sentences.en: the communist regime that had ruled Hungary since the end of the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 自二战结束以来统治匈牙利的共产主义政权的民众起义爆发的三天后。

sentences.en: And the revolution was originally inspired by intellectuals and students, so people with a lot of polo necks.
sentences.zh: 这场革命最初是由知识分子和学生，也就是穿着高领毛衣的人发起的。

sentences.en: You can't leave it alone, can you?
sentences.zh: 你就是放不下这个梗，对吧？

sentences.en: I can't.
sentences.zh: 我放不下。

sentences.en: Even when they're heroic and fighting for freedom.
sentences.zh: 即使是在他们表现得很英勇、为自由而战的时候。

sentences.en: It's just a knee-jerk thing now.
sentences.zh: 这现在纯粹是一种条件反射了。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: They're protesting against general repression and censorship, but then it became
sentences.zh: 他们抗议普遍的镇压和审查制度，但随后它

sentences.en: amalgamated with the anger of factory workers and peasants, people who had terrible working
sentences.zh: 与工厂工人和农民的愤怒融合在了一起，这些人有着糟糕的工作

sentences.en: and housing conditions, low wages, high prices, and they felt that they were just downtrodden and they weren't being heard.
sentences.zh: 和居住条件、低工资、高物价，他们觉得自己饱受压迫却无人倾听。

sentences.en: And it shot through with this sense of Hungarian patriotism, fury at their leader's slavish loyalty to the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 这其中交织着强烈的匈牙利爱国主义，以及对他们的领导人奴性地效忠苏联的愤怒。

sentences.en: And that, of course, was symbolized by the presence on Hungarian soil of so many Soviet troops.
sentences.zh: 当然，这由驻扎在匈牙利领土上的大量苏联军队象征性地体现出来。

sentences.en: So last time, two successive Stalinist leaders, Matthias Rakowski and Erna Gera, were kicked out.
sentences.zh: 所以上一次，两任斯大林主义领导人，马加什·拉科西和格罗·埃尔诺，被赶下台。

sentences.en: And the man at the top, your hero, this sort of walrus-moustached, family grocer lookalike,
sentences.zh: 而最高领导人，你的英雄，这种海象胡须、长得像杂货铺老板似的人物，

sentences.en: Imran Nodz, Mr. Big.
sentences.zh: 伊姆雷·纳吉，大人物。

sentences.en: And Nodz, to remind people, he's a very sort of stolid, dogged man.
sentences.zh: 为了提醒大家，纳吉是一个非常稳重、顽强的人。

sentences.en: He's a party loyaliSt. He wants to save socialism, restore order.
sentences.zh: 他是一名坚定的党内忠诚者。他想要拯救社会主义，恢复秩序。

sentences.en: He is also a moderate who has been arguing for a kinder, gentler, more authentically Hungarian path to socialism.
sentences.zh: 他也是一个温和派，一直主张走一条更温和、更友善、更具匈牙利本土特色的社会主义道路。

sentences.en: So Nodz has been pulled in different directions.
sentences.zh: 所以纳吉一直在被不同的力量拉扯。

sentences.en: And spoiler alert, the tension between those two things will have tragic consequences for him.
sentences.zh: 剧透一下，这两者之间的紧张关系将为他带来悲剧性的后果。

sentences.en: So as we heard last time, on the morning of the 24th of October,
sentences.zh: 正如我们上次听到的，在 10 月 24 日的早晨，

sentences.en: Nikita Khrushchev, the kind of paramount leader of the Soviet Union, ordered the Red Army to move into Budapest and restore order.
sentences.zh: 苏联的最高领导人尼基塔·赫鲁晓夫下令红军进驻布达佩斯并恢复秩序。

sentences.en: They run into heavy resistance on the streets.
sentences.zh: 他们在街头遇到了强烈的抵抗。

sentences.en: They lost five tanks and 120 men that first day.
sentences.zh: 他们在第一天就损失了五辆坦克和 120 名士兵。

sentences.en: And so as night falls on the 25th, the second day, there are massive crowds on the streets.
sentences.zh: 因此，随着 25 日（第二天）夜幕降临，街上挤满了大量民众。

sentences.en: They're singing the national anthem, waving these Hungarian flags with the communist emblem cut out.
sentences.zh: 他们在唱国歌，挥舞着剪掉了共产主义标志的匈牙利国旗。

sentences.en: And they are building barricades in preparation for the Soviet attack.
sentences.zh: 他们正在修建街垒，为苏军的进攻做准备。

sentences.en: Now, we've talked almost entirely about Budapest, but actually this is now a nationwide uprising.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们几乎一直在谈论布达佩斯，但实际上这现在是一场全国性的起义。

sentences.en: So in cities and towns across Hungary, there are big demonstrations.
sentences.zh: 因此，在匈牙利各地的城市和小镇，都有大型示威活动。

sentences.en: And they unite people of all classes.
sentences.zh: 它们团结了各个阶层的人。

sentences.en: So workers, peasants, policemen, intellectuals, public officials, army officers, and so on.
sentences.zh: 工人和农民、警察、知识分子、公职人员、军队军官等等。

sentences.en: And in the cities, people are producing independent newspapers.
sentences.zh: 在城市里，人们在制作独立报纸。

sentences.en: They've taken over radio stations.
sentences.zh: 他们接管了广播电台。

sentences.en: Workers have taken over factories.
sentences.zh: 工人们接管了工厂。

sentences.en: They're organising public transport themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们自己组织公共交通。

sentences.en: They're organising workers' councils, so kind of taking charge of people's food, all of this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 他们组织了工人委员会，某种程度上接管了人们的食物供应，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And in the countryside, the peasants in the villages are organising food supplies into
sentences.zh: 而在乡村，村里的农民正组织向

sentences.en: Budapest to support the revolutionaries.
sentences.zh: 布达佩斯运送粮食供应，以支援革命者。

sentences.en: So Simon Hall, in his book on 1956, quotes a building worker who was driving through rural Western Hungary on the 26th of October.
sentences.zh: 因此，西蒙·霍尔在他关于 1956 年的书里，引用了一名建筑工人的话，这名工人在 10 月 26 日开车穿过匈牙利西部乡村。

sentences.en: And this building worker said, wherever he drove, he could see people flying Hungarian flags in the villages and peasants huddled
sentences.zh: 这名建筑工人说，无论他开车到哪里，他都能看到人们在村子里挂着匈牙利国旗，农民们聚集

sentences.en: around the single radio set in the village to try to find out what was going on.
sentences.zh: 在村里仅有的收音机周围，试图弄清楚发生了什么。

sentences.en: And as he points out in his book, Simon Hall, there are often big differences between the workers in the cities and the peasants in the countryside.
sentences.zh: 正如西蒙·霍尔在他的书中指出的那样，城市工人和乡村农民之间往往存在很大差异。

sentences.en: But what seems to unite all of these different people is the single word freedom.
sentences.zh: 但将所有这些不同的人团结在一起的，似乎是“自由”这一个词。

sentences.en: That's the word that comes up again and again.
sentences.zh: 这是那个一次又一次被提及的词。

sentences.en: And it has different meanings.
sentences.zh: 它有着不同的含义。

sentences.en: Freedom of speech, freedom of assembly, political freedom, or simply national freedom from what they see as the Soviet jackboot.
sentences.zh: 言论自由、集会自由、政治自由，或者仅仅是从他们眼中苏军铁蹄下获得的国家自由。

sentences.en: Now, of course, all revolutions
sentences.zh: 当然，所有的革命

sentences.en: have different sides to them.
sentences.zh: 都有不同的一面。

sentences.en: We've done however many episodes on the French Revolution.
sentences.zh: 我们关于法国大革命已经做过不知多少集节目了。

sentences.en: There's idealism and enthusiasm, but there's also often a spirit of destruction.
sentences.zh: 其中有理想主义和热情，但也往往伴随着一种破坏精神。

sentences.en: And this is true in
sentences.zh: 这一点在

sentences.en: 1956 as well.
sentences.zh: 1956 年也是如此。

sentences.en: So by this point, there were reports from across Hungary of people destroying statues and war memorials, tearing down the red stars from buildings, breaking into communist party
sentences.zh: 所以到这个时候，匈牙利各地都有报道称，人们在摧毁雕像和战争纪念碑，撕下大楼上的红星，闯入共产党

sentences.en: or secret police headquarters and things.
sentences.zh: 或秘密警察总部之类的机构。

sentences.en: And this is not a bloodless revolution.
sentences.zh: 这不是一场没有流血的革命。

sentences.en: Far from it.
sentences.zh: 远非如此。

sentences.en: It's the most famous incident.
sentences.zh: 这是最著名的一次事件。

sentences.en: On the afternoon of Saturday, the 27th of October,
sentences.zh: 在 10 月 27 日星期六的下午，

sentences.en: Western journalists were taken across the border from Austria to a little town of, Tom?
sentences.zh: 西方记者被带过奥地利边境，来到一个小镇，汤姆，叫什么？

sentences.en: Moson Magyarovar.
sentences.zh: 莫松马扎尔古瓦尔（Mosonmagyarovar）。

sentences.en: Not bad.
sentences.zh: 还不错。

sentences.en: I mean, well, not good, to be fair.
sentences.zh: 我是说，好吧，说实话也不算太好。

sentences.en: I think it's Moson Magyarovar.
sentences.zh: 我觉得是莫松马扎尔古瓦尔。

sentences.en: It's a very long word, but it's got Magyar in it.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常长的词，但里面有“马扎尔”这个词。

sentences.en: So I know what that means.
sentences.zh: 所以我知道那是什么意思。

sentences.en: That means Hungarian.
sentences.zh: 那意思是匈牙利人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But you know what?
sentences.zh: 但你知道吗？

sentences.en: Magyar is actually pronounced Modjor.
sentences.zh: “Magyar”实际上发音是 Modjor。

sentences.en: Is it?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: Who knew?
sentences.zh: 谁知道呢？

sentences.en: They did.
sentences.zh: 他们知道。

sentences.en: Viktor Orban knew, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 我想维克托·欧尔班是知道的。

sentences.en: Yeah, he'd know.
sentences.zh: 对，他会知道。

sentences.en: And indeed, the new leader of Hungary, who's called, we call Peter Magyar, but I think they would call...
sentences.zh: 而且确实，匈牙利的新领导人，他的名字叫，我们叫彼得·马扎尔（Peter Magyar），但我认为他们会叫……

sentences.en: Modja.
sentences.zh: 莫佳。

sentences.en: Modjor.
sentences.zh: 莫焦尔。

sentences.en: Anyway, wow.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，哇。

sentences.en: I mean, you learn a lot on the rest of this history, don't you?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你在本期历史节目中学到了很多，不是吗？

sentences.en: People must be astounded how much they're learning.
sentences.zh: 人们一定对他们学到了这么多东西感到震惊。

sentences.en: When it's delivered with such authority, that's what people really like about the show.
sentences.zh: 当它以如此权威的方式表达出来时，这正是人们真正喜欢这个节目的地方。

sentences.en: They could rely on us.
sentences.zh: 他们可以信任我们。

sentences.en: All these journalists are taken to Moson Magyarovar, and they're taken to the mortuary, which is crowded with bodies.
sentences.zh: 所有这些记者都被带到了莫松马扎尔古瓦尔，他们被带到了挤满尸体的停尸房。

sentences.en: And the reason it's crowded with bodies is this.
sentences.zh: 它挤满尸体的原因是这样的。

sentences.en: The day before, a thousand people had marched on the secret police headquarters in this little town to demand the removal of the communist red star.
sentences.zh: 就在前一天，有一千人游行到这个小镇的秘密警察总部，要求拆除共产主义红星。

sentences.en: They said, take the red star down and put the Hungarian flag up.
sentences.zh: 他们说，把红星摘下来，挂上匈牙利国旗。

sentences.en: And the secret police commander at first seemed willing to talk, and he was talking to the crowd.

sentences.zh: 所以他收到了来自米高扬和苏斯洛夫在布达佩斯的最新报告。

sentences.en: Podcasting gold.
sentences.zh: 当赫鲁晓夫看到它时，他并没有觉得，哦，太棒了，这以完美的方式结束了。

sentences.en: So he's had his latest report from Mikoyan and Suslov in BudapeSt.
sentences.zh: 他觉得这糟透了。

sentences.en: And when Khrushchev looks at it, he doesn't think, oh, brilliant, this has ended wonderfully.
sentences.zh: 共产党基本上已经土崩瓦解了。

sentences.en: He thinks this is terrible.
sentences.zh: 匈牙利全国各地的工厂都已经停工。

sentences.en: The Communist Party has basically fallen apart.
sentences.zh: 他们想夺取政权

sentences.en: The factories across Hungary have shut down.
sentences.zh: 反革命分子正在抬头

sentences.en: Newspapers and radio stations have been taken over by rebels.
sentences.zh: 报社和广播电台已经被叛军接管了。

sentences.en: And I quote,
sentences.zh: 我是原话引述：

sentences.en: The political situation in the country and in Budapest is not getting better.
sentences.zh: 国内以及布达佩斯的政治局势没有好转。

sentences.en: It is getting worse.
sentences.zh: 情况正在恶化。

sentences.en: That's not all.
sentences.zh: 还不止于此。

sentences.en: At this point, Khrushchev has almost certainly, we can't be sure, but almost certainly had reports of another massacre, this time in Budapest on the morning of the 30th of October.
sentences.zh: 在这个时候，赫鲁晓夫几乎可以肯定——虽然我们无法百分之百确定，但几乎可以肯定——已经收到了又一起大屠杀的报告，这一次发生在10月30日早上的布达佩斯。

sentences.en: And basically, what happened in this massacre, there were a group of revolutionaries that laid siege to the headquarters of the Budapest kind of municipal communist party,
sentences.zh: 基本上，这场大屠杀的起因是一群革命者包围了布达佩斯某种市政共产党总部，

sentences.en: which was occupied by secret police and party officials.
sentences.zh: 该总部当时被秘密警察和党政官员占据。

sentences.en: The secret police started shooting at them, and they hit some bystanders in the crowd, including women.
sentences.zh: 秘密警察开始向他们开枪，并击中了人群中的一些旁观者，其中包括女性。

sentences.en: Then there was a massive gun battle.
sentences.zh: 随后爆发了一场激烈的枪战。

sentences.en: And the boss of the Budapest party, who was a friend of Imre Nodge, a close friend of Nodge, he brokered a ceasefire.
sentences.zh: 布达佩斯党组织负责人、伊姆雷·纳吉的朋友、纳吉的密友出面斡旋了一场停火。

sentences.en: But while he was trying to organize a kind of full surrender and the evacuation of the building, insurgents broke into the building and they shot him and they shot his bodyguards.
sentences.zh: 但正当他试图组织全面投降和大楼人员撤离时，起义者冲进大楼，枪杀了他和他的保镖。

sentences.en: And then there was this horrendous scene where the people in the building, most of whom were young army officers or young secret police officers, were led outside.
sentences.zh: 接着发生了极其恐怖的一幕，大楼里的人——其中大部分是年轻的军官或年轻的秘密警察——被押到了外面。

sentences.en: It was captured by a photojournalist from Life magazine, a British journalist called John Sadovi.
sentences.zh: 这一幕被《生活》杂志的一位英国战地摄影记者约翰·萨多维捕捉到了。

sentences.en: And you can see his pictures online and they are pretty, you know, haunting.
sentences.zh: 你可以在网上看到他的照片，它们非常、你知道的，触目惊心。

sentences.en: These very young men are led outside.
sentences.zh: 这些非常年轻的男子被带到外面。

sentences.en: Most of them are clearly, absolutely terrified.
sentences.zh: 他们大多数人显然都惊恐万分。

sentences.en: And they are shot in cold blood in full view of the cameras at point blank range.
sentences.zh: 他们在摄像机的众目睽睽之下、在极近的距离被冷血枪杀。

sentences.en: Just 23 of them are shot in all.
sentences.zh: 总共有23人被枪杀。

sentences.en: Their bodies were beaten and mutilated and then they were strung up.
sentences.zh: 他们的尸体遭到殴打和虐待，然后被悬挂起来。

sentences.en: Again, in full view of the cameras from trees and from lampposts and people spat on their bodies.
sentences.zh: 同样是在摄像机的众目睽睽之下，被挂在树上和路灯杆上，人们还在他们的尸体上吐口水。

sentences.en: As Sadovi, the photojournalist said, I'd spent three years in the war, meaning Second World War, but nothing I saw then could compare with the horror of this.
sentences.zh: 正如摄影记者萨多维所说：“我在战争中度过了三年，指的是第二次世界大战，但我当时看到的任何东西都无法与这恐怖景象相比。”

sentences.en: So Khrushchev has almost certainly got this report about this massacre happening to kind of party officials.
sentences.zh: 因此，赫鲁晓夫几乎可以肯定收到了关于这场针对党政官员的大屠杀的报告。

sentences.en: Khrushchev is not a stranger to violence.
sentences.zh: 赫鲁晓夫对暴力并不陌生。

sentences.en: It's not like he's, you know, he's a shrinking violet or something.
sentences.zh: 他可不是什么，你知道的，胆小怕事的人。

sentences.en: But this plays on his mind, as does the fact that he's getting messages from other communist countries to say, what on earth is going on in Hungary?
sentences.zh: 但这让他感到忧心忡忡，正如他不断收到其他共产主义国家发来的消息一样，他们质问匈牙利到底在搞什么鬼？

sentences.en: So the Chinese, for example, are saying, oh, you lost your minds.
sentences.zh: 所以，比如中国就在说，哦，你们疯了。

sentences.en: You know, Hungary is in complete chaos.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，匈牙利已经彻底陷入混乱。

sentences.en: You're doing nothing about it.
sentences.zh: 你们什么也没做。

sentences.en: And even more significantly, the other countries of the Warsaw Pact.
sentences.zh: 更重要的是华沙条约组织的其它成员国。

sentences.en: You know, Czechoslovakia, Romania and so on, East Germany.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，捷克斯洛伐克、罗马尼亚等等，还有东德。

sentences.en: They're very worried.
sentences.zh: 他们非常担心。

sentences.en: If you open the door to multi-party elections in Hungary, well, people will want them in Poland.
sentences.zh: 如果你在匈牙利打开多党选举的大门，那么，波兰人也会要求多党选举。

sentences.en: They want them in Czechoslovakia.
sentences.zh: 他们会在捷克斯洛伐克要求选举。

sentences.en: There are reports already of student protests in some of these places, most notably Romania, which has a big ethnic Hungarian minority population.
sentences.zh: 已经有报道称其中一些地方爆发了学生抗议活动，最引人注目的是罗马尼亚，那里有庞大的匈牙利族少数群体人口。

sentences.en: There have been student protests in the city in the west of Romania, not far from Hungary, called Timisoara,
sentences.zh: 在罗马尼亚西部靠近匈牙利的一个叫蒂米什瓦拉的城市，爆发了学生抗议活动，

sentences.en: actually a city that plays a massive part in the eventual revolution in 1989 and clashes with the security forces and so on.
sentences.zh: 这座城市实际上在1989年的最终革命中发挥了巨大作用，其中包括与安全部队的冲突等等。

sentences.en: So the Kremlin is under pressure from all these people.
sentences.zh: 因此克里姆林宫承受来自所有这些人的压力。

sentences.en: And also when they look at it, they say they see everything in terms of the wider balance of power.
sentences.zh: 而且当他们审视局势时，他们总是从更广泛的力量对比来看待一切。

sentences.en: So Christophe now, when they're all assembled there, he says to his colleagues, if we withdraw from Hungary, this would encourage the American, British and French imperialists.
sentences.zh: 所以现在克鲁晓夫当他们都在那里集合时，他对同僚们说：“如果我们从匈牙利撤军，这将鼓励美、英、法帝国主义者。”

sentences.en: They would interpret it as a sign of our weakness and they would go on to attack and our party would not understand us.
sentences.zh: 他们会把这视为我们软弱的信号，他们会继续进攻，我们的党也不会理解我们。

sentences.en: Besides Egypt, we would be giving away Hungary too.
sentences.zh: 除了埃及，我们还要把匈牙利也拱手让人。

sentences.en: So we have no other choice but to intervene.
sentences.zh: 所以我们别无选择，只能干预。

sentences.en: So in other words, this goes back to your point, Tom, that as with the British in Suez, the motivation is if we don't do this, we look weak and then we lose the rest of our empire.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这就回到了你的观点，汤姆，正如英国人在苏伊士运河一样，动机是如果我们不这样做，我们就会显得软弱，然后我们就会失去帝国的其余部分。

sentences.en: What will other people think of us?
sentences.zh: 别人会怎么看我们？

sentences.en: We don't want to necessarily get stuck in, but we feel like we have to.
sentences.zh: 我们不一定想卷入其中，但我们觉得自己不得不这么做。

sentences.en: And of course, because Suez has kicked off now, that does make Khrushchev's task a little bit easier.
sentences.zh: 当然，由于苏伊士运河事件已经爆发，这确实让赫鲁晓夫的任务变得容易了一些。

sentences.en: The West are divided and distracted.
sentences.zh: 西方国家分裂且分心。

sentences.en: The Americans have basically massively fallen out with Britain and France.
sentences.zh: 美国人基本上和英法彻底闹翻了。

sentences.en: So if we were ever going to crack down on Hungary, this is the time.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们打算镇压匈牙利，现在就是时机。

sentences.en: They would have done it, though, do you think, anyway, even if Suez hadn't been going on?
sentences.zh: 不过你觉得，即使没有苏伊士运河的事情发生，他们无论如何也会这么做吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think they might have done it later, but I think they would have done it anyway.
sentences.zh: 我想他们可能会晚一点动手，但我想他们无论如何都会这么做的。

sentences.en: So Khrushchev says to his colleagues, okay, forget what we said about withdrawing troops.
sentences.zh: 所以赫鲁晓夫对同僚们说：“好吧，忘掉我们之前关于撤军的言论吧。”

sentences.en: Let us take the initiative in restoring order.
sentences.zh: 让我们带头恢复秩序。

sentences.en: We will flood Hungary with troops in the next few days.
sentences.zh: 我们将在接下来的几天里用军队淹没匈牙利。

sentences.en: I want this to be led by another Second World War veteran, Marshal Ivan Konyev.
sentences.zh: 我希望由另一位二战老兵伊万·科涅夫元帅来领导这次行动。

sentences.en: We will crush the revolution.
sentences.zh: 我们要粉碎这场革命。

sentences.en: We'll find a new Hungarian leader, not just a waste of space.
sentences.zh: 我们要找一个真正的匈牙利领导人，而不是一个无能之辈。

sentences.en: Let's get someone we can really truSt.
sentences.zh: 让我们找一个我们真正能信任的人。

sentences.en: Now, there is one person who really disagrees with him about all this.
sentences.zh: 现在，有一个人对此持强烈反对意见。

sentences.en: And this is Anastas Mikoyan, ice cream guy, ice cream, Armenian.
sentences.zh: 这就是阿纳斯塔斯·米高扬，那个卖冰淇淋的家伙，卖冰淇淋的亚美尼亚人。

sentences.en: He flew in that night from Budapest, and he is stunned when he realizes that they have decided to invade.
sentences.zh: 他那天夜里从布达佩斯飞来，当他意识到他们已经决定入侵时，他惊呆了。

sentences.en: After midnight, Mikoyan rang Khrushchev at home, and he said, basically got him out of bed.
sentences.zh: 午夜过后，米高扬给家里的赫鲁晓夫打电话，基本上把他从床上叫了起来。

sentences.en: He said, what are you doing?
sentences.zh: 他说，你在干什么？

sentences.en: Let's have another meeting.
sentences.zh: 我们再开个会吧。

sentences.en: I want to make my case.
sentences.zh: 我想陈述我的理由。

sentences.en: We should not use force.
sentences.zh: 我们不应该使用武力。

sentences.en: I'm dead set against this whole thing.
sentences.zh: 我坚决反对整件事情。

sentences.en: And Khrushchev said to him, look, we've made the decision.
sentences.zh: 赫鲁晓夫对他说：“听着，我们已经做出了决定。”

sentences.en: We've established the timetable.
sentences.zh: 我们已经制定了时间表。

sentences.en: And we'd have to rip up the timetable for intervention if we meet again.
sentences.zh: 如果我们再次开会，我们就得撕毁干预的时间表。

sentences.en: Our whole plan would be ruined.
sentences.zh: 我们的整个计划都会泡汤。

sentences.en: I personally think we made the right decision, and you're wrong.
sentences.zh: 我个人认为我们做出了正确的决定，而你错了。

sentences.en: And then he hangs up.
sentences.zh: 然后他挂断了电话。

sentences.en: Communists, they love a plan.
sentences.zh: 共产党人，他们太爱制定计划了。

sentences.en: Yeah, but it's interesting, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是的，但这很有趣，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because I think a lot of people think of the communist leadership as top-down, repressive, monolithic.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为很多人认为共产党领导层是自上而下、压制性的、铁板一块的。

sentences.en: Monolithic.
sentences.zh: 铁板一块。

sentences.en: And here they're ringing each other at midnight, having sort of shouting matches.
sentences.zh: 而在这里，他们在午夜互相打电话，进行某种激烈的争吵。

sentences.en: Even more.
sentences.zh: 甚至更甚。

sentences.en: Khrushchev gets up the next morning.
sentences.zh: 赫鲁晓夫第二天早上起床。

sentences.en: He lives like someone of them do in the Sparrow Hills above Moscow.
sentences.zh: 他和其他人一样住在莫斯科上空的麻雀山上。

sentences.en: He gets up the next morning.
sentences.zh: 他第二天早上起床。

sentences.en: He walks to his car, which is a kind of zeal black limousine at the end of the drive.
sentences.zh: 他走向他的汽车，那是车道尽头的一辆吉尔黑色豪华轿车。

sentences.en: And who's by the car?
sentences.zh: 谁在车旁？

sentences.en: Mikoyan, who lives basically next door.
sentences.zh: 米高扬，基本上就住在隔壁。

sentences.en: And Mikoyan says to him, before you get in the car, I'm telling you, this is a terrible mistake.
sentences.zh: 米高扬对他说：“在你上车之前，我告诉你，这是一个可怕的错误。”

sentences.en: It will undermine the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 这会破坏苏联的根基。

sentences.en: It will undermine the image of communism.
sentences.zh: 这会损害共产主义的形象。

sentences.en: If blood is shed, I don't know what I'll do with myself, Mikoyan says.
sentences.zh: 如果流血了，我都不知道自己该怎么办，米高扬说。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, he's behaving better than Macmillan did.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，他的表现比麦克米伦要好。

sentences.en: Or Selwyn Lloyd.
sentences.zh: 或者塞尔温·劳埃德。

sentences.en: Yeah, he is the Harold Macmillan of this story, but he's behaving much better.
sentences.zh: 是的，他是这个故事里的哈罗德·麦克米伦，但他的表现要好得多。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's absolutely true.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全没错。

sentences.en: Well, actually, there's another candidate to be the Harold Macmillan, which we'll come to in a second.
sentences.zh: 其实，还有另一个人选来扮演哈罗德·麦克米伦的角色，我们一会儿就会讲到。

sentences.en: And Khrushchev says to him, look, you know, everybody else is telling us we've got to do this.
sentences.zh: 赫鲁晓夫对他说：“听着，你知道的，其他所有人都在告诉我们必须这么做。”

sentences.en: The Poles, the Czechoslovaks, the Romanians, the Bulgarians, even Tito's telling us we've got to do this.
sentences.zh: 波兰人、捷克斯洛伐克人、罗马尼亚人、保加利亚人，甚至铁托都告诉我们必须这么做。

sentences.en: Do you think this is easy for me?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这对我来说容易吗？

sentences.en: Khrushchev says.
sentences.zh: 赫鲁晓夫说。

sentences.en: We have to act.
sentences.zh: 我们必须采取行动。

sentences.en: We have no other choice.
sentences.zh: 我们别无选择。

sentences.en: And then he gets in the car and off he goes to work.
sentences.zh: 然后他上了车，去上班了。

sentences.en: Now, already, rumours of the decision have started to reach BudapeSt.
sentences.zh: 现在，关于这个决定的传言已经开始传到布达佩斯。

sentences.en: So as early as the 31st of October, there were reports that Soviet engineers were building bridges across the river Tiso that motorised units were crossing into Hungary from the
sentences.zh: 早在10月31日，就有报道称苏联工兵正在蒂萨河上架设桥梁，摩托化部队正从

sentences.en: border with what's now Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 现在属于乌克兰的边界进入匈牙利。

sentences.en: And by the next day, the 1st of November, there are more reports.
sentences.zh: 到了第二天，即11月1日，有更多的报道。

sentences.en: Soviet troops, far from returning to their barracks, are actually moving in to secure the airports.
sentences.zh: 苏联军队不仅没有返回军营，反而开进并控制了机场。

sentences.en: And there are tanks and thousands of reinforcements now coming across the borders from Ukraine and Romania.
sentences.zh: 现在有坦克和数千名增援部队正从乌克兰和罗马尼亚的边境涌入。

sentences.en: And that morning, Nodz calls in the Soviet ambassador, Yuri Andropov, and he says, what's all this?
sentences.zh: 那天早上，纳吉召见了苏联大使尤里·安德罗波夫，他说，这都是怎么回事？

sentences.en: What's going on?
sentences.zh: 到底在搞什么鬼？

sentences.en: Andropov is totally impassive, not an unfamiliar thing with a Soviet or Russian ambassador.
sentences.zh: 安德罗波夫完全面无表情，对于苏联或俄罗斯大使来说，这并不罕见。

sentences.en: He's totally kind of stone-faced.
sentences.zh: 他完全是一副面无表情的样子。

sentences.en: And he says, just troop movements.
sentences.zh: 他说，只是调动军队。

sentences.en: Yeah, routine troop movements before we withdraw all our troops from your country.
sentences.zh: 是的，在我们从你们国家撤出所有军队之前的例行调动。

sentences.en: And Nodz says, I'm not sure you're telling me the truth.
sentences.zh: 纳吉说，我并不确信你对我说的是实话。

sentences.en: And if you don't stop this, we will leave the Warsaw Pact immediately.
sentences.zh: 如果你不停止这种行为，我们将立即退出华沙条约组织。

sentences.en: And later that afternoon, they've now got confirmation Red Army is crossing the border in force.
sentences.zh: 那天下午晚些时候，他们现在得到了红军大举越境的证实。

sentences.en: Nodz meets his cabinet, and they all agree, fine, we're going to withdraw from the Warsaw
sentences.zh: 纳吉会见了内阁成员，他们一致同意，好吧，我们要退出华沙条

sentences.en: Pact.
sentences.zh: 约。

sentences.en: We're going to declare Hungary a neutral country.
sentences.zh: 我们要宣布匈牙利为中立国。

sentences.en: And they call Andropov back to tell him at five o'clock.
sentences.zh: 他们在五点钟把安德罗波夫叫回来告诉他这个决定。

sentences.en: What do they think is going to happen?
sentences.zh: 他们以为会发生什么？

sentences.en: Do they seriously think that they can just slip the Soviet leash like that?
sentences.zh: 他们真的以为自己可以就这样摆脱苏联的控制吗？

sentences.en: It's really hard to say.
sentences.zh: 这真的很难说。

sentences.en: So it's often said, you see it repeated often in sort of popular accounts.
sentences.zh: 所以人们经常这样说，你经常在一些通俗的叙述中看到这种重复。

sentences.en: The Red Army intervened to stop them leaving the Warsaw Pact.
sentences.zh: 红军干预是为了阻止他们退出华沙条约组织。

sentences.en: That's not right.
sentences.zh: 这不对。

sentences.en: They only said they wanted to leave the Warsaw Pact after they knew the Red Army were about to attack them.
sentences.zh: 他们只是在得知红军即将进攻后，才说想要退出华沙条约组织。

sentences.en: And I think the point of them doing this, I think in an odd way, Nodz thinks this might reassure the Kremlin.

sentences.zh: 他出生时，母亲跟着父亲回到了匈牙利。

sentences.en: And she was trying to persuade his father to do the decent thing and marry her.
sentences.zh: 她试图说服父亲做个体面的男人并娶她。

sentences.en: But he refused.
sentences.zh: 但他拒绝了。

sentences.en: So, she ended up living in a little village near Lake Bolaton with her son, Janosz.
sentences.zh: 所以她最后带着儿子亚诺什住在巴拉顿湖附近的一个小村庄里。

sentences.en: And they were very poor.
sentences.zh: 他们非常穷。

sentences.en: And at the end of the First World War, she moved to Budapest and got work as a cleaner.
sentences.zh: 第一次世界大战结束后，她搬到布达佩斯靠做清洁工谋生。

sentences.en: And little Janosz, he left school at 14.
sentences.zh: 小亚诺什14岁就辍学了。

sentences.en: He worked as a servant for a pig herder.
sentences.zh: 他曾在一个养猪场当过佣工。

sentences.en: He worked as a newspaper boy and a delivery boy.
sentences.zh: 他当过送报童和送货员。

sentences.en: Then he was homeless for a bit.
sentences.zh: 接着他流落街头了一段时间。

sentences.en: And then he became an apprentice typewriter repairer.
sentences.zh: 后来他成了一名打字机修理学徒。

sentences.en: Then in 1928, Janosz won a chess tournament.
sentences.zh: 然后在1928年，亚诺什赢得了一场国际象棋比赛。

sentences.en: He was 16 years old.
sentences.zh: 他当时16岁。

sentences.en: And his prize was a book by Friedrich Engels called Anti-During.
sentences.zh: 他的奖品是弗里德里希·恩格斯写的一本书，叫《反杜林论》。

sentences.en: Oh, goody, goody, mummy.
sentences.zh: 哦，太棒了，好极了，妈咪。

sentences.en: Look what I've been given.
sentences.zh: 看看我得到了什么。

sentences.en: And it was an explanation.
sentences.zh: 这是一本阐述理论的书。

sentences.en: Anti-During basically tries to establish Marxism as a scientific creed to prove the scientific truth of Marxism.
sentences.zh: 《反杜林论》基本上试图将马克思主义确立为一种科学的信条，以证明马克思主义的科学真理姓。

sentences.en: When he lost his job in the Depression, he became a full-time communist activiSt.
sentences.zh: 当他在大萧条中失业后，他成了一名全职的共产主义活动家。

sentences.en: He was in and out of prison.
sentences.zh: 他多次进出监狱。

sentences.en: And his alias, he decided to take the alias Kupa, which in Hungarian is Kadar.
sentences.zh: 至于他的化名，他决定使用库帕这个化名，在匈牙利语里就是卡达尔。

sentences.en: So this is how he became Janosz Kadar.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是他如何成为亚诺什·卡达尔的。

sentences.en: And he became very close to this bloke, Roik.
sentences.zh: 他与这家伙罗伊克变得非常亲密。

sentences.en: They became great pals, and they were promoted together to the Hungarian Politburo at the end of the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 他们成了好朋友，并在二战结束后一起晋升为匈牙利政治局委员。

sentences.en: Now, there's a really interesting description of Kadar.
sentences.zh: 现在，有一段对卡达尔非常有趣的描述。

sentences.en: I mentioned already a bloke called Sir Brian Cartlidge, who was the British ambassador to
sentences.zh: 我之前提到过一个叫布莱恩·卡特利奇爵士的家伙，他曾是英国驻

sentences.en: Hungary and also to the Soviet Union in the 80s, I think.
sentences.zh: 匈牙利大使，我想在80年代也担任过驻苏联大使。

sentences.en: And he wrote, has written this sort of definitive English language history of Hungary from start to finish.
sentences.zh: 他写过一本关于匈牙利从头到尾的权威英语历史书。

sentences.en: Massive book.
sentences.zh: 一本厚重的大书。

sentences.en: And he met Kadar.
sentences.zh: 他见过卡达尔。

sentences.en: And he's really interesting about him.
sentences.zh: 他对卡达尔的评价非常有趣。

sentences.en: He says, Kadar was a personally very modest man.
sentences.zh: 他说，卡达尔是一个为人非常谦逊的人。

sentences.en: He was low-key.
sentences.zh: 他很低调。

sentences.en: He spoke quietly and simply.
sentences.zh: 他说话轻声细语、朴实无华。

sentences.en: Kadar didn't think of himself as an intellectual.
sentences.zh: 卡达尔不认为自己是个知识分子。

sentences.en: He genuinely saw himself as the kind of spokesman for the ordinary working people of Hungary.
sentences.zh: 他真心实意地把自己看作是匈牙利普通劳动人民的代言人。

sentences.en: And Cartlidge said of Kadar, the key to him was not ideological Marxism.
sentences.zh: 卡特利奇谈到卡达尔时说，理解他的关键不是意识形态上的马克思主义。

sentences.en: It wasn't his loyalty to the ideology, but his loyalty to the institution, to the party, the true protector, or so he believed, of the interests and well-being of the Hungarian
sentences.zh: 关键不在于他对意识形态的忠诚，而在于他对机构、对党的忠诚，他坚信党是匈牙利人民利益和福祉的真正保护者。

sentences.en: people.
sentences.zh: 人民。

sentences.en: So every other consideration, quote, including those of morality and personal honour, were subordinate for Kadar to the interests of the party.
sentences.zh: 因此，对卡达尔来说，所有其他考虑，包括道德和个人荣誉的考虑，都必须服从于党的利益。

sentences.en: So this is the guy who has vanished.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个后来失踪的人。

sentences.en: What had happened to him was this.
sentences.zh: 在他身上发生的事情是这样的。

sentences.en: When he left that emotional meeting where he said, I'd rather die, you know, I will die if Russian troops invade our country.
sentences.zh: 当他离开那场充满情绪的会议时，他说过，我宁愿死，你知道，如果苏联军队入侵我们的国家，我会死。

sentences.en: The other bloke, Munich, said to him, I'm going to the Soviet embassy.
sentences.zh: 另一个人，明尼奇对他说，我要去苏联大使馆。

sentences.en: I think you should come with me and we can continue this conversation with the Soviet ambassador.
sentences.zh: 我认为你应该跟我一起去，我们可以继续与苏联大使交谈。

sentences.en: They went to the Soviet embassy and there, Andropov said to them, look, I'm going to level with you.
sentences.zh: 他们去了苏联大使馆，在那里，安德罗波夫对他们说，听着，我对你们开诚布公吧。

sentences.en: We are going to invade your country.
sentences.zh: 我们打算入侵你们国家。

sentences.en: And it's a fait accompli.
sentences.zh: 这是既成事实。

sentences.en: There's nothing you can do to stop it.
sentences.zh: 你们对此无可奈何，也阻止不了。

sentences.en: Nod's game is up and he is done for, he said.
sentences.zh: 纳吉的大势已去，他完蛋了，他说。

sentences.en: And Andropov said, listen, I'll tell you what I'll do.
sentences.zh: 安德罗波夫说，听着，我告诉你们我能做什么。

sentences.en: I'll fly you to Moscow.
sentences.zh: 我用飞机送你们去莫斯科。

sentences.en: You can come with me.
sentences.zh: 你们可以跟我一起去。

sentences.en: You can talk to the Presidium yourselves in the Kremlin.
sentences.zh: 你们可以亲自在克里姆林宫与主席团交谈。

sentences.en: You can tell them what you think is going on in Hungary and you can help us as Soviet friends to sort it out.
sentences.zh: 你们可以把你们对匈牙利局势的看法告诉他们，并作为苏联的朋友协助我们解决问题。

sentences.en: And they said, OK, you know, who knows what's going on in Kadar's mind there when he gets on that plane.
sentences.zh: 他们说，好吧，你知道，当卡达尔登上那架飞机时，谁知道他心里在想什么。

sentences.en: But anyway, he gets on the plane.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，他上了飞机。

sentences.en: They fly to Moscow.
sentences.zh: 他们飞往莫斯科。

sentences.en: They land in Moscow.
sentences.zh: 他们在莫斯科降落。

sentences.en: They're driven straight to the Kremlin to meet Khrushchev and the Presidium.
sentences.zh: 他们被直接车送到克里姆林宫去见赫鲁晓夫和主席团。

sentences.en: And as Victor Sebastian says in his fun book, I mean, it's weird to say fun book, but it's a really dramatic book about the Hungarian revolution.
sentences.zh: 正如维克托·塞巴斯蒂安在他的那本有趣的书中所说，我的意思是，说是一本有趣的书有点奇怪，但这是一本关于匈牙利革命的极其戏剧性的书。

sentences.en: Effectively, what's happening here is the Presidium are interviewing him for a job as the new dictator of Hungary.
sentences.zh: 实际上，这里发生的事情是主席团正在面试他，看他是否适合担任匈牙利的新独裁者。

sentences.en: But Kadar doesn't seem to realize this because he's unbelievably honest with them.
sentences.zh: 但卡达尔似乎并没有意识到这一点，因为他对他们诚实得令人难以置信。

sentences.en: They say, well, what do you think about the revolution?
sentences.zh: 他们说，好吧，你对这场革命怎么看？

sentences.en: He says, well, to be honest, I kind of was for it because I'm a Hungarian patriot.
sentences.zh: 他说，嗯，老实说，我其实挺支持它的，因为我是个匈牙利爱国者。

sentences.en: And, you know, I felt like we had to make some changes.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我觉得我们必须做出一些改变。

sentences.en: And everybody in Hungary, he says, wants to see your troops out.
sentences.zh: 他说，匈牙利的每个人都希望看到你们的军队撤出。

sentences.en: We want to see the back of the Red Army, me included.
sentences.zh: 我们希望红军滚蛋，包括我在内。

sentences.en: He said to them, they said, well, we're about to invade.
sentences.zh: 他对他们说，对方说，好吧，我们正准备入侵。

sentences.en: And he said, well, I think that's a very bad idea.
sentences.zh: 他说，嗯，我认为这是个非常糟糕的主意。

sentences.en: Don't send in the tanks.
sentences.zh: 不要派遣坦克进去。

sentences.en: I quote, if you do this, the morale of the communists will be reduced to zero.
sentences.zh: 我原话引述，如果你这样做，共产主义者的士气将降至零。

sentences.en: If order in Hungary is restored by force, the authority of the socialist countries will be eroded.
sentences.zh: 如果用武力恢复匈牙利的秩序，社会主义国家的威信将会受到侵蚀。

sentences.en: See how much he cares.
sentences.zh: 看看他有多在乎。

sentences.en: Always he's thinking about what's good for socialism, what's good for the party.
sentences.zh: 他脑子里想的永远是对社会主义有利的事，对党有利的事。

sentences.en: And how do the Russians take this?
sentences.zh: 那俄罗斯人对此作何反应？

sentences.en: Well, they're not, I mean, they're not pleased to hear this, right?
sentences.zh: 好吧，他们，我的意思是，他们听到这话可高兴不起来，对吧？

sentences.en: Because he's telling them that what they're doing is wrong.
sentences.zh: 因为他在告诉他们，他们正在做的事情是错误的。

sentences.en: Khrushchev is still not sure.
sentences.zh: 赫鲁晓夫仍然拿不定主意。

sentences.en: Is this guy the man?
sentences.zh: 这家伙是我们要找的人吗？

sentences.en: Khrushchev speaks to Tito.
sentences.zh: 赫鲁晓夫跟铁托谈了谈。

sentences.en: And Tito says, oh, obviously you should pick this guy.
sentences.zh: 铁托说，哦，显然你应该选这家伙。

sentences.en: The fact that this guy has stood up to you a little bit, you know, that's exactly what you want.
sentences.zh: 这家伙居然敢顶撞你们一点，你知道，这正是你们想要的。

sentences.en: This guy, people in Hungary will say he's patriotic.
sentences.zh: 这家伙，匈牙利人会说他很爱国。

sentences.en: He was tortured.
sentences.zh: 他曾经遭受过酷刑。

sentences.en: He was smeared in mercury and people urinated in his mouth.
sentences.zh: 他被涂抹水银，人们还在他嘴里撒尿。

sentences.en: People in Hungary know this and they won't see him as just a Stalinist puppet.
sentences.zh: 匈牙利人知道这一点，他们不会把他仅仅看作一个斯大林的傀儡。

sentences.en: They know that he has suffered and they will give him a little bit of leeway because of it.
sentences.zh: 他们知道他受过苦，正因为如此，他们会对他多一点宽容。

sentences.en: So the obvious question is, why does Kardar himself go along with this?
sentences.zh: 所以显而易见的问题是，为什么卡达尔本人会同意这样做？

sentences.en: Is this just treachery from him?
sentences.zh: 这纯粹是他的背叛吗？

sentences.en: Lots of listeners may say, well, he sounds like a terrible person.
sentences.zh: 许多听众可能会说，听起来他是个糟糕透顶的人。

sentences.en: It's like kind of Marshall Pétain.
sentences.zh: 这有点像贝当元帅那样。

sentences.en: I suppose you could see it that way.
sentences.zh: 我想你可以这么看。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, both Pétain and Kardar would say, I mean, by the way, I despise Pétain, but both of them would say, well, country's on its knees.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，贝当和卡达尔都会说，顺便说一句，我鄙视贝当，但他们两个都会说，国家已经陷入绝境。

sentences.en: We were going to lose anyway.
sentences.zh: 横竖都是输。

sentences.en: Country's on its knees.
sentences.zh: 国家已经陷入绝境。

sentences.en: Somebody had to step up and do the dirty work to try to bring us back.
sentences.zh: 总得有人站出来做脏活，试图挽救我们。

sentences.en: And I think reading about him, his reputation in Hungary today is very contested, but there are a lot of people, actually, who are remarkably sympathetic to him.
sentences.zh: 我想阅读有关他的资料会发现，他在今天的匈牙利声誉饱受争议，但实际上有很多人对他异常同情。

sentences.en: I mean, lots of critics, of course, but there are a lot of people who are also very sympathetic to him.
sentences.zh: 当然有很多批评者，但也有很多人对他非常同情。

sentences.en: And they would say, listen, he knows the revolution is doomed.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，听着，他知道革命注定要失败。

sentences.en: He just wants to do the best of the party and he wants to rebuild his country.
sentences.zh: 他只是想为党做最好的事，他想重建他的国家。

sentences.en: So Kardar was in Moscow.
sentences.zh: 所以卡达尔当时在莫斯科。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, in Budapest, the tension is at fever pitch.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在布达佩斯，紧张气氛达到了白热化。

sentences.en: So by the evening of the 2nd of November, the Red Army has encircled the city, but the
sentences.zh: 因此到11月2日傍晚，红军已经包围了这座城市，但

sentences.en: Red Army commanders are still keeping up pretense that this is going to be solved by negotiations.
sentences.zh: 红军指挥官仍在伪装，假装这一切将通过谈判解决。

sentences.en: And in fact, the next morning on the 3rd of November, senior Soviet commanders arrived at the Hungarian parliament.
sentences.zh: 事实上，第二天早晨11月3日，苏联高级指挥官抵达了匈牙利议会。

sentences.en: They said, we just come to chat about the withdrawal of all our troops from your country.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我们只是来聊聊从你们国家撤走所有军队的事。

sentences.en: In fact, the talks actually went quite well.
sentences.zh: 事实上，会谈进行得相当顺利。

sentences.en: And they said, well, we'll continue the talks this evening at Soviet military headquarters.
sentences.zh: 他们说，今晚我们将在苏联军事总部继续会谈。

sentences.en: At the Tukul base, which is south of BudapeSt.
sentences.zh: 在布达佩斯以南的特克尔基地。

sentences.en: And the Hungarians sent their military officers, their own commanders to this base.
sentences.zh: 匈牙利人派出了他们的军官和自己的指挥官前往这个基地。

sentences.en: And of course, you know what's going to happen.
sentences.zh: 当然，你们知道会发生什么。

sentences.en: They walked in, they started the negotiations.
sentences.zh: 他们走了进去，开始谈判。

sentences.en: Clang.
sentences.zh: 当啷。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Just before midnight, door opens and a load of Soviet KGB men walk in with carrying submachine guns and they are under the personal command of the Soviet KGB chief, Ivan Serov.
sentences.zh: 午夜刚过，门开了，一大群苏联克格勃特工走了进来，携带著冲锋枪，他们由苏联克格勃主管伊万·谢罗夫亲自指挥。

sentences.en: And these Hungarian commanders are all put under arreSt.
sentences.zh: 这些匈牙利指挥官全部被捕。

sentences.en: And just a few hours later, 4 a.m., Marshal Konev issues the signal Thunder 444, which is the code word to trigger Operation Whirlwind.
sentences.zh: 仅仅几个小时后，即凌晨4点，科涅夫元帅下达了代号为“雷霆444”的信号，这是发动“旋风行动”的暗号。

sentences.en: And this is the basically the final occupation of BudapeSt.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是对布达佩斯的最后占领。

sentences.en: So immediately 60,000 Red Army troops and thousands of tanks begin to move into the city.
sentences.zh: 因此，6万名红军部队和数千辆坦克立即开始驶入这座城市。

sentences.en: And within an hour, they are closing in on the city center.
sentences.zh: 一个小时内，他们就逼近了市中心。

sentences.en: They are meeting some resistance as they did before.
sentences.zh: 他们遇到了一些抵抗，就像之前一样。

sentences.en: But this time they have come in such an overwhelming numbers and they are absolutely determined they're not going to be taking any prisoners.
sentences.zh: 但这一次，他们以压倒性的人数蜂拥而入，并且绝对决心不留任何活口。

sentences.en: Now, Nodz could have ordered the Hungarian army onto the streets to resist them, to fight back.
sentences.zh: 现在，纳吉本可以下令匈牙利军队走上街头进行抵抗、发起反击。

sentences.en: But he decides not to.
sentences.zh: 但他决定不这样做。

sentences.en: He decides it's pointless.
sentences.zh: 他认为这毫无意义。

sentences.en: We're outnumbered.
sentences.zh: 我们寡不敌众。

sentences.en: We're outgunned.
sentences.zh: 我们火力不如人。

sentences.en: I don't want to waste people's lives.
sentences.zh: 我不想白白牺牲人们的生命。

sentences.en: And at 5.19 in the morning, he goes on the state radio.
sentences.zh: 早上5点19分，他在国家广播电台发表讲话。

sentences.en: You can hear the gunfire in the background as he's talking.
sentences.zh: 当他说话时，你可以听到背景中的枪声。

sentences.en: And he says, this is the president of the Council of Ministers of the Hungarian People's
sentences.zh: 他说，这是匈牙利人民共和国部长会议主席。

sentences.en: Republic.
sentences.zh: 共和国。

sentences.en: Today at daybreak, Soviet forces launched an attack on our capital with the obvious intention of overthrowing the legal democratic Hungarian government.
sentences.zh: 今天天刚亮，苏联军队对我们的首都发动了进攻，其明显意图是推翻合法的匈牙利民主政府。

sentences.en: Our troops are fighting.
sentences.zh: 我们的军队正在战斗。

sentences.en: The government is in its place.
sentences.zh: 政府各就各位。

sentences.en: I am notifying the people of our country and the world.
sentences.zh: 我正在向我们国家和世界人民发出通告。

sentences.en: So a little bit kind of Vladimir Zelensky, February 2022 kind of vibe to this.
sentences.zh: 这有点像弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基在2022年2月的那种氛围。

sentences.en: You know, the government is in its place.
sentences.zh: 你知道，政府坚守岗位。

sentences.en: I'm not going anywhere.
sentences.zh: 我哪儿也不去。

sentences.en: But the difference is that Kiev held out in 2022, but Soviet troops are closing in very quickly on the parliament in BudapeSt.
sentences.zh: 但不同的是，基辅在2022年坚守住了，而苏联军队正以极快的速度逼近布达佩斯的议会大厦。

sentences.en: So a couple of hours later, Nod and his family and about 30 of his close colleagues accepted an offer of sanctuary at the Yugoslavian embassy.
sentences.zh: 因此几个小时后，纳吉和他的家人以及大约30名亲密同事接受了南斯拉夫大使馆的避难提议。

sentences.en: At eight o'clock, Soviet tanks entered the parliament square and at 8.07, Radio Koshut, the state radio broadcast its last message.
sentences.zh: 八点钟，苏联坦克开进议会广场，8点07分，科舒特广播电台——国家广播电台播出了最后一条消息。

sentences.en: It was a woman's voice.
sentences.zh: 那是一个女人的声音。

sentences.zh: 这跟塞得港的英法联军比起来怎么样？

sentences.en: So anyway, by the evening of that first day, Konev's troops control most of the major buildings and intersections and stuff in BudapeSt.

sentences.zh: 他们又坚持了几天，但苏军对他们进行了猛烈的狂轰滥炸。

sentences.zh: 商店、公寓楼、教堂、医院，甚至还有一家儿童诊所。

sentences.zh: 街道上尸横遍野。

sentences.zh: 当时，那里的记者中有一位是共产党员，一个名叫彼得·弗赖尔的英国共产党员，他当时在为大不列颠

sentences.zh: 共产党机关报《每日工人报》做报道。

sentences.zh: 当他把这篇和其他报道发回《每日工人报》时，他们不仅拒绝刊登，编辑甚至不让其他员工看一眼。

sentences.en: And Fryer was so horrified by this that he left the paper and, of course, the Communist Party in proteSt.
sentences.zh: 弗赖尔对此感到震惊万分，于是愤而辞职，离开了这家报社，当然也退出了共产党。

sentences.zh: 所以有大量令人心碎的呼吁。

sentences.zh: 这是维也纳监听站在11月4日下午截获的另一个。

sentences.zh: 这是另一个叛军广播电台的最后一条消息。

sentences.en: Civilized people of the world, on the watchtower of 1,000-year-old Hungary, the last flames begin to go out.
sentences.zh: 世界文明人啊，在拥有千年历史的匈牙利瞭望塔上，最后的火焰开始熄灭了。

sentences.en: Soviet tanks and guns are roaring over Hungarian soil.
sentences.zh: 苏联的坦克和火炮正在匈牙利的土地上轰鸣。

sentences.en: Our women are sitting in dread.
sentences.zh: 我们的妇女在恐惧中瑟瑟发抖。

sentences.en: They still have terrible memories of the Red Army in 1945.
sentences.zh: 她们对1945年的红军仍心有余悸。

sentences.en: Save our souls.
sentences.zh: 救救我们的灵魂吧。

sentences.en: But by the 11th of November, the guns have fallen silent.
sentences.zh: 但到了11月11日，枪声已经平息。

sentences.en: The revolution is definitively over.
sentences.zh: 革命彻底结束了。

sentences.en: So about 2,700 Hungarians have been killed in the Soviet attack.
sentences.zh: 在苏联的进攻中，大约有2700名匈牙利人丧生。

sentences.en: More than half of those are civilians, 200 of them children, and tens of thousands injured.
sentences.zh: 其中一半以上是平民，有200名儿童，还有数万人受伤。

sentences.en: The Red Army lost about 700 men killed.
sentences.zh: 红军阵亡约700人。

sentences.en: There's also a massive kind of refugee exodus.
sentences.zh: 同时还有大规模的难民出逃潮。

sentences.en: So about 200,000 people fled the country across the borders into Austria or Yugoslavia.
sentences.zh: 大约有20万跨越国境逃往奥地利或南斯拉夫。

sentences.en: Some of them ended up in Britain and other European countries, but most of them ended up in Canada and the United States.
sentences.zh: 他们中有些人最终去了英国和其他欧洲国家，但大多数人去了加拿大和美国。

sentences.en: Now, what's the rest of the world been doing?
sentences.zh: 那么，世界其他地方在干什么呢？

sentences.en: The rest of the world has been watching in horror and doing absolutely nothing, really.
sentences.zh: 世界其他地方一直在惊恐地旁观，实际上什么也没做。

sentences.en: So there are big demonstrations across Europe in most capitals.
sentences.zh: 欧洲大部分首都都爆发了大型游行。

sentences.en: There are attacks on Soviet embassies in some very unexpected places, in Luxembourg, in Iceland, in Switzerland, and so on.
sentences.zh: 在一些非常意想不到的地方，比如卢森堡、冰岛、瑞士等，发生了袭击苏联大使馆的事件。

sentences.en: There were lots of offers of help for Hungarian refugees.
sentences.zh: 有许多提供帮助匈牙利难民的提议。

sentences.en: So in Simon Hall's book, he describes some nice British examples, heartwarming British examples.
sentences.zh: 西蒙·霍尔在他的书中描述了一些美好的英国例子，温暖人心的英国例子。

sentences.en: So there was a place called Donington Hall in Leicestershire.
sentences.zh: 莱斯特郡有个地方叫多宁顿庄园。

sentences.en: It's a big country house that turned itself into a camp for 150 Hungarian children.
sentences.zh: 这是一座大型乡村宅邸，被改造成了容纳150名匈牙利儿童的营地。

sentences.en: There was a building firm in Wolverhampton, which built a free house, semi-detached house for a Hungarian family.
sentences.zh: 沃尔夫汉普顿有一家建筑公司，为一户匈牙利家庭建造了一栋免费的半独立式房屋。

sentences.en: So much Wolverhampton history.
sentences.zh: 太多的沃尔夫汉普顿历史了。

sentences.en: So much Wolverhampton in this, but some would say not enough, frankly.
sentences.zh: 这里有太多沃尔夫汉普顿的影子，但坦白说，有人会觉得还不够。

sentences.en: I mean, if you obviously listen to the bonus series, you've had a bit extra, but I think we could have had more.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你显然听了特别节目，你已经了解了一些额外内容，但我认为我们本可以了解更多。

sentences.en: At the end of the year, Time magazine picked the Hungarian freedom fighter as man of the year, so the Hungarians fought bravely against the most brutal tyranny on earth
sentences.zh: 年底，《时代》杂志将匈牙利自由斗士评为年度风云人物，匈牙利人勇敢地与地球上最残暴的暴政进行了抗争，

sentences.en: and have shaken history's greatest despotism to its foundations.
sentences.zh: 并动摇了历史上最大专制统治的根基。

sentences.en: That answer, you ended up being Kermit the Frog's voice.
sentences.zh: 那个回答，你最后听起来成了青蛙科米特的嗓音。

sentences.zh: 不，听起来真的很不错。

sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.zh: 这把20世纪50年代冷战战士的模仿绝了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Now, the most famous example of solidarity with the Hungarians, the most sort of sentimental story, comes at the Melbourne Olympics.
sentences.zh: 现在，最著名的声援匈牙利人的例子，也就是那种最感人的故事，发生在墨尔本奥运会上。

sentences.en: So a bit of Australian history on the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 所以在播客里讲点澳大利亚历史。

sentences.en: And this is actually one of the most celebrated moments in the history of the Olympics.
sentences.zh: 这其实是奥运会历史上最著名的时刻之一。

sentences.en: So it's the blood-in-the-water water polo match.
sentences.zh: 也就是水中血战水球赛。

sentences.en: Are you familiar with this match, Tom?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你熟悉这场比赛吗？

sentences.en: I'm ashamed to say I'm not.
sentences.zh: 我很羞愧地说，我不熟悉。

sentences.en: So it was the semi-final of the water polo, and the Hungarians were playing the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 这是水球半决赛，匈牙利对阵苏联。

sentences.en: Oh, goodness.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: It was a kind of Hungarian-Australians in the crowd.
sentences.zh: 观众席里有很多匈牙利裔澳大利亚人。

sentences.en: It was a very, very raucous occasion, and it turned violent in the pool, which is why it was called blood-in-the-water.
sentences.zh: 那是一个非常喧闹的场合，水池里爆发了暴力冲突，这也是它被称为水中血战的原因。

sentences.en: The Hungarians won 4-0, turned into a massive brawl, including the crowd.
sentences.zh: 匈牙利人以4比0获胜，演变成了一场包括观众在内的大规模群殴。

sentences.en: And the Hungarians went on to win the gold medal, and half of the team promptly defected, refused to go home.
sentences.zh: 匈牙利人随后赢得了金牌，半数队员随即叛逃，拒绝回国。

sentences.en: So it's been made into a film, two films, actually, this story, one of which was shown to George W.
sentences.zh: 所以这个故事被拍成了电影，其实是两部，其中一部还在白宫放给乔治·W·

sentences.en: Bush in the White House.
sentences.zh: 布什看过了。

sentences.en: The obvious question is why – I mean, it's all very well to have these fine words and water polo crowds, but why didn't the West give them any practical help?
sentences.zh: 显而易见的问题是，为什么——我是说，这些漂亮的言辞和水球观众的呐喊倒是不错，但为什么西方不给他们提供切实的帮助呢？

sentences.en: Third World War?
sentences.zh: 第三次世界大战？

sentences.en: Third World War, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然是为了第三次世界大战。

sentences.en: For the Hungarians, though, this played into a familiar theme.
sentences.zh: 然而对匈牙利人来说，这契合了一个熟悉的主题。

sentences.en: So in 1848-49, they'd risen against the Habsburgs.
sentences.zh: 所以在1848至1849年，他们曾奋起反抗哈布斯堡王朝。

sentences.en: Their revolution was then crushed by Russian intervention in 1849.
sentences.zh: 他们的革命随后在1849年被俄国的干涉镇压了。

sentences.en: Well, we will be exploring the life of the Tsar who commanded that.
sentences.zh: 我们将会探讨那位下达命令的沙皇的一生。

sentences.zh: 尼古拉一世，对吧？

sentences.en: Nicholas I, the gendarme of Europe.
sentences.zh: 尼古拉一世，欧洲宪兵。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So the Hungarians, to some extent, this is a familiar story for them.
sentences.zh: 所以对匈牙利人来说，在某种程度上，这是一个熟悉的故事。

sentences.en: You know, they try to rise up.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们试图奋起反抗。

sentences.en: People offer, you know, well-meaning sentiments, but they don't offer practical help.
sentences.zh: 人们表达了，你知道的，好意的同情，但他们不提供实际的帮助。

sentences.en: I mean, I suppose the Iranians might say the same.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想伊朗人可能也会这么说。

sentences.en: I think there are probably quite a few people who might say the same, actually.
sentences.zh: 我想实际上可能还有相当多的人会这么说。

sentences.en: Chinese in 1989, right?
sentences.zh: 比如1989年的中国人，对吧？

sentences.en: So what was Eisenhower doing in all this?
sentences.zh: 那么艾森豪威尔在这一切中在做什么呢？

sentences.en: Eisenhower actually told her Secretary of State, John Foster Duller, send a message to Moscow and tell Moscow, we do not see the Hungarians as potential allies.
sentences.zh: 艾森豪威尔实际上对她的国务卿约翰·福斯特·杜勒斯说，给莫斯科发个消息，告诉莫斯科，我们不认为匈牙利人是潜在盟友。

sentences.en: Don't worry, we are not behind all this.
sentences.zh: 别担心，我们不是在这一切背后操纵。

sentences.en: You know, we're not doing this as a balance of power move against you, all of this.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们这不是在对你搞势力均衡的举动，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Now, of course, as the Hungarians themselves said, looked a little bit hypocritical, because the Americans, all through the late 40s and 50s,
sentences.zh: 当然，正如匈牙利人自己所说，这显得有点虚伪，因为美国人在整个40年代末和50年代一直在谈论他们将如何帮助东欧的沦陷国家，

sentences.en: had been talking about how they would help the captive nations of Eastern Europe, and yet when it came to it, they would do nothing.
sentences.zh: 然而真到了关键时刻，他们却什么也不做。

sentences.en: This is actually what John Foster Dulles himself said in late October.
sentences.zh: 这其实正是约翰·福斯特·杜勒斯本人在10月下旬所说的话。

sentences.en: Dulles said to his colleagues in Washington, it will be said that here are the great moments, and when they came and these fellows were ready to stand up and die,
sentences.zh: 杜勒斯对华盛顿的同事们说，人们会说这是重大历史时刻，而当它们到来、这些家伙准备挺身而出英勇牺牲时，

sentences.en: we were caught napping and we did nothing.
sentences.zh: 我们却在打瞌睡，什么也没做。

sentences.en: I think he's not necessarily wrong.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他这话不无道理。

sentences.en: So the West did nothing, the revolution lost, and what happened next, just to tie up the story?
sentences.zh: 所以西方什么也没做，革命失败了，接下来发生了什么，好给这个故事收尾？

sentences.en: So Kadar and Munich, the turncoats, had been flown into Eastern Hungary on the morning of the 4th, after the operation to retake Budapest had begun.
sentences.zh: 因此，叛徒卡达尔和慕尼黑在4号早晨、在收复布达佩斯的行动开始后，被空运到了匈牙利东部。

sentences.en: Kadar read a radio address to the Hungarian people.
sentences.zh: 卡达尔向匈牙利人民发表了电台讲话。

sentences.en: He said,
sentences.zh: 他说：

sentences.en: The revolution began, you know, it's an honest and patriotic thing, but it's been taken over by reactionaries and fascists,
sentences.zh: 革命开始了，你知道的，这是一件诚实和爱国的事情，但它被反动分子和法西斯分子窃取了，

sentences.en: so I'm assuming power at the head of an emergency worker-peasant government.
sentences.zh: 所以我将以紧急工农政府首脑的身份接管政权。

sentences.en: I've asked the Red Army to help us crush the sinister forces of reaction, and after that, I promise the Red Army will leave.
sentences.zh: 我已请求红军帮助我们粉碎反动派的险恶势力，在那之后，我保证红军会离开。

sentences.en: And he was then escorted into Budapest by Soviet tanks, sworn in as prime minister and installed in the parliament building,
sentences.zh: 随后他在苏联坦克的护送下进入布达佩斯，宣誓就任总理并入驻议会大厦，

sentences.en: which has actually survived relatively unscathed from gunfire.
sentences.zh: 大厦在枪林弹雨中其实保存得相对完好。

sentences.en: Now, at first, Kadar's authority and credibility are pretty much non-existent.
sentences.zh: 起初，卡达尔的权威和信誉几乎荡然无存。

sentences.en: So he basically tries to win over people by appearing to be moderate.
sentences.zh: 所以他基本上试图通过表现得温和来赢得人心。

sentences.en: In his first big speech, he promises them higher wages.
sentences.zh: 在他的第一次大型演讲中，他承诺提高工资。

sentences.en: He's saying,
sentences.zh: 他说：

sentences.en: I'll bring in a national holiday celebrating the heroes of 1848.
sentences.zh: 我要设立一个纪念1848年英雄的国定假日。

sentences.en: He makes a series of other promises.
sentences.zh: 他还做了一系列其他承诺。

sentences.en: He says, don't worry, I won't bring back the secret police.
sentences.zh: 他说，别担心，我不会把秘密警察带回来。

sentences.en: And there won't be any witch hunt against the people who were in the revolution.
sentences.zh: 也不会对参加过革命的人进行任何政治迫害。

sentences.en: And actually, when the dust has settled, Kadar says, we can have a multi-party system, and I'd love to have us.
sentences.zh: 事实上，等尘埃落定后，卡达尔说，我们可以实行多党制，我很乐意看到这样。

sentences.en: I'd love to see us have free elections.
sentences.zh: 我很乐意看到我们举行自由选举。

sentences.en: That'd be really nice.
sentences.zh: 那真的会很好。

sentences.en: And what about the Nojsta?
sentences.zh: 那纳吉呢？

sentences.en: The Nojsta is still in the Yugoslav embassy.
sentences.zh: 纳吉仍然在南斯拉夫大使馆里。

sentences.en: He's sheltering the Yugoslav embassy.
sentences.zh: 他在南斯拉夫大使馆避难。

sentences.en: And Kadar says, listen, you know, I know that the Nojsta didn't want this to all go down as it did.
sentences.zh: 卡达尔说，听着，你知道的，我知道纳吉并不希望事情变成现在这样。

sentences.en: He is absolutely free to come out.
sentences.zh: 他完全可以自由出来。

sentences.en: We won't pursue him.
sentences.zh: 我们不会追究他。

sentences.en: He should just come out and retire to private life.
sentences.zh: 他只要出来过退休生活就行了。

sentences.en: And obviously, no one would do anything to him.
sentences.zh: 显然没有人会对怎么样他。

sentences.en: Now, does Kadar mean this?
sentences.zh: 那卡达尔是认真的吗？

sentences.en: It's really impossible to say whether this is completely disingenuous or whether he's later reacting to pressure.
sentences.zh: 实在很难说这完全是虚伪，还是他后来对压力作出的反应。

sentences.en: But what definitely happens is this.
sentences.zh: 但毫无疑问发生的是：

sentences.en: He doesn't fulfill any of these promises.
sentences.zh: 他没有兑现这些承诺中的任何一个。

sentences.en: He does bring back the secret police.
sentences.zh: 他确实把秘密警察带回来了。

sentences.en: He begins to crack down on dissidents within weeks.
sentences.zh: 他在几周内就开始镇压异见人士。

sentences.en: And above all, Kadar agrees to a Soviet plan to winkle Noj out of the Yugoslav embassy.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，卡达尔同意了一项苏联计划，要把纳吉从南斯拉夫大使馆诱骗出来。

sentences.en: He sends Tito a letter.
sentences.zh: 他给铁托写了一封信。

sentences.en: And he says, look, if Noj and his friends come out, we will give them a safe conduct back to their families.
sentences.zh: 他说，听着，如果纳吉和他的朋友们出来，我们将保证他们安全回到家人身边。

sentences.en: So on the 22nd of November, Noj and Co.
sentences.zh: 于是11月22日，纳吉一行人

sentences.en: leave the Yugoslav embassy and they get on this big bus.
sentences.zh: 离开了南斯拉夫大使馆，登上了这辆大巴。

sentences.en: And to their horror, it turns out the bus has been organized by the KGB.
sentences.zh: 令他们惊恐的是，这辆大巴居然是克格勃安排的。

sentences.en: They're driven to a military academy.
sentences.zh: 他们被驱车送到一所军事学院。

sentences.en: They're told to get off the bus and then they're flown to Romania.
sentences.zh: 他们被命令下车，然后被空运到了罗马尼亚。

sentences.en: And in Romania, they're held under house arreSt.
sentences.zh: 在罗马尼亚，他们被软禁了起来。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, so we're now well into the autumn and winter of 1956.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，我们现在已经进入了1956年的深秋和冬季。

sentences.en: Kadar is coming under pressure from other communist governments.
sentences.zh: 卡达尔正受到其他共产党政府的压力。

sentences.en: Can you crack down a bit more, please?
sentences.zh: 拜托，能不能再严厉一点打击？

sentences.en: Crack down harder.
sentences.zh: 打击力度再大一点。

sentences.en: In fact, in January 1957, a load of other Warsaw Pact leaders visited Budapest and said, we've come here to show solidarity with you, but also to encourage you.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在1957年1月，一大批华沙条约组织领导人访问了布达佩斯，并表示，我们来这里是为了表达对你们的声援，也是为了鼓励你们。

sentences.en: Stamp out all dissent, please.
sentences.zh: 拜托，铲除所有异见。

sentences.en: So he does as he's encouraged.
sentences.zh: 于是他照着鼓励去做了。

sentences.en: He bans non-communist parties.
sentences.zh: 他取缔了非共产党派别。

sentences.en: He bans workers' councils.
sentences.zh: 他取缔了工人委员会。

sentences.en: He shuts down the Writers' Association.
sentences.zh: 他关闭了作家协会。

sentences.en: Oh, he's having a crack at the poets.
sentences.zh: 哦，他开始找诗人们的麻烦了。

sentences.en: He's having a crack at the poets, exactly.
sentences.zh: 他开始找诗人们的麻烦了，没错。

sentences.en: And he sets up new people's courts to try people for political offences with the power of imposing the death penalty.
sentences.zh: 并且他建立了新的“人民法院”，以审判政治犯，并拥有判处死刑的权力。

sentences.en: And the most high-profile victim.
sentences.zh: 而最受瞩目的受害者是——

sentences.en: No!
sentences.zh: 不！

sentences.en: I hate to break this to you.
sentences.zh: 我实在不忍心打破你的幻想。

sentences.en: Not Nodj.
sentences.zh: 不是纳吉。

sentences.en: Our old friend, Imre Nodj, friend of the show.
sentences.zh: 我们的老朋友，伊姆雷·纳吉，节目老熟人了。

sentences.en: Oh, dear.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: He's for the chop, I'm afraid.
sentences.zh: 恐怕他难逃一死了。

sentences.en: So it was always thought that Kadar moved against him because he was under pressure from the Kremlin.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们一直认为卡达尔对付他是因为受到了来自克里姆林宫的压力。

sentences.en: But actually, in his book, Victor Sebastian makes the case that actually Kadar decided to get rid of him himself.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，维克托·塞巴斯蒂安在他的书中指出，其实是卡达尔决定亲自除掉他。

sentences.en: Because Kadar thought, I will never be secure.
sentences.zh: 因为卡达尔觉得：我永远不会安全。

sentences.en: Order and stability will never be entrenched as long as the Nodjster is out there inspiring people with his charisma and his powers of oratory.
sentences.zh: 只要纳吉还在外面用他的个人魅力和雄辩才能鼓舞人心，秩序与稳定就永远无法巩固。

sentences.en: So, in March 1957, Hungarian police travelled to Romania and they arrested Nodj and co and they brought them all back to BudapeSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，在1957年3月，匈牙利警察前往罗马尼亚逮捕了纳吉等人，并把他们全部押回了布达佩斯。

sentences.en: Now, Kadar couldn't quite decide, he dithered for months, couldn't decide what to do with Nodj.
sentences.zh: 现在，卡达尔拿不定主意，他犹豫了好几个月，不知道该拿纳吉怎么办。

sentences.en: Nodj would not confess.
sentences.zh: 纳吉拒不认罪。

sentences.en: He wouldn't admit that he'd done anything wrong.
sentences.zh: 他不承认自己做错了任何事。

sentences.en: So a show trial was a bad idea.
sentences.zh: 所以搞一场摆样子的公开审判是个坏主意。

sentences.en: So eventually, they put him on trial behind closed doors for treason.
sentences.zh: 因此最终，他们秘密对其实施了审判，罪名是叛国。

sentences.en: The verdict, of course, is a foregone conclusion and poor old Nodj is sentenced to death.
sentences.zh: 判决结果当然是板上钉钉，可怜的纳吉被判处死刑。

sentences.en: And he gives a very dignified, moving, final statement.
sentences.zh: 他发表了一份非常庄严、感人的最后陈述。

sentences.en: Why don't you read his final statement, Tom, since you're such a big fan of the man?
sentences.zh: 托姆，既然你是他的超级粉丝，不如由你来读读他的最后陈述吧？

sentences.en: My sole solace is my conviction that sooner or later the Hungarian people and the international working class will exonerate me of the grave accusations,
sentences.zh: 我唯一的慰藉是坚信，迟早有一天匈牙利人民和国际工人阶级会洗清强加给我的严重罪名，

sentences.en: as a consequence of which I must sacrifice my life.
sentences.zh: 为此我不得不牺牲自己的生命。

sentences.en: But I offer it willingly.
sentences.zh: 但我甘愿奉献。

sentences.en: After all that has happened, it has no value any longer.
sentences.zh: 经历了这一切之后，生命已毫无价值。

sentences.en: I realise that there will be another Imre Nodj trial at which I shall be rehabilitated.
sentences.zh: 我意识到还会有一场针对伊姆雷·纳吉的审判，到那时我将获得平反。

sentences.en: And three times as many people will come to my re-interment as went to Reich's.
sentences.zh: 出席我重新安葬仪式的人数将是赖克葬礼的三倍。

sentences.en: My only dread is that my eulogy will be given by those who betrayed me.
sentences.zh: 我唯一的恐惧是，致悼词的将是那些背叛了我的人。

sentences.en: See, I think you could.
sentences.zh: 你看，我觉得你完全可以。

sentences.en: If you'd done that in a different voice, it would be really moving.
sentences.zh: 如果你换个声线来读，这其实会非常感人。

sentences.en: But he's quite moving.
sentences.zh: 但他读得挺感人的。

sentences.en: I mean, he's a, you know, he's a drab guy who has no powers of oratory whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他是个……你知道的，是个毫无口才可言的沉闷家伙。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But it's still moving.
sentences.zh: 但它依然感人。

sentences.en: He's a dogged and decent man who tried to do his beSt.
sentences.zh: 他是个顽强正派、尽力而为的人。

sentences.en: Do you want me to give it a bit more zip?
sentences.zh: 你想让我把它读得更有活力一点吗？

sentences.en: No, I think you've made your choice.
sentences.zh: 不，我想你已经做出了选择。

sentences.en: You've made your dramatic choice and you've got to own it.
sentences.zh: 你做出了戏剧性的选择，就必须承担到底。

sentences.en: I think it's great to have a drab, uncharismatic figure at the centre of such dramatic events.
sentences.zh: 我觉得在这样惊心动魄的事件中心，有一个沉闷、毫无个人魅力的形象，这感觉棒极了。

sentences.en: And I don't think it diminishes the pathos of his end.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这会削弱他结局的悲剧色彩。

sentences.en: Hungarian listeners who are poised to write in and complain, listen to what Tom just said.
sentences.zh: 那些准备写信来抱怨的匈牙利听众们，听听托姆刚才说了什么。

sentences.en: Tom is saying that this terrible impression that he gave is actually to Nodj's credit.
sentences.zh: 托姆是在说，他刚才那糟糕的模仿实际上反衬出纳吉的功绩。

sentences.en: And that just shows how much we value him.
sentences.zh: 这恰恰说明了我们有多看重他。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, a lack of charisma in many ways is an appealing characteristic in a politician, I think.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在很多方面，缺乏个人魅力反而是政客身上一种讨人喜欢的特质，我认为。

sentences.en: So Keir Starmer joins us on the show.
sentences.zh: 所以基尔·斯塔默加入了我们的节目。

sentences.en: It's the charismatic politicians who are always the dangerous ones.
sentences.zh: 那些总是充满个人魅力的政客才往往是危险人物。

sentences.en: You're not wrong there.
sentences.zh: 你这话倒没说错。

sentences.en: So anyway, Nodj and two of his colleagues were hanged on the 16th of June, 1958, and they were buried face down in an unmarked grave.
sentences.zh: 所以无论如何，纳吉和他的两名同事于1958年6月16日被绞死，并被脸朝下埋在了一个无名墓穴中。

sentences.en: Very sad.
sentences.zh: 非常悲惨。

sentences.en: And there were some of 341 people executed in five years after 1956 as Kadar tightened his grip.
sentences.zh: 在1956年之后的五年里，随着卡达尔收紧对权力的控制，大约有341人被处决。

sentences.en: There were 20,000 people imprisoned or interned, tens of thousands of people lost their jobs, and some were even deported to the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 有两万人被监禁或拘禁，数万人失业，甚至还有人被流放到苏联。

sentences.en: And yet the paradox is that Kadar did crack down, and he did execute people and put people in prison.
sentences.zh: 然而矛盾的是，卡达尔确实进行了镇压，也确实处决了人并把人关进监狱。

sentences.en: And yet at the same time, his version of communism was much more moderate than what had gone before.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，他版本的共产主义比以往要温和得多。

sentences.en: So he's trying to win the Hungarian people over.
sentences.zh: 因此，他正试图争取匈牙利人民的支持。

sentences.en: He gives them pay increases.
sentences.zh: 他给他们加薪。

sentences.en: He borrows a lot of money abroad to try to improve their living standards.
sentences.zh: 他在国外借了大量资金，试图提高他们的生活水平。

sentences.en: And by about 1962, so that's about five or six years after the revolution, he's adopted a much more conciliatory line.
sentences.zh: 到1962年左右，也就是革命爆发后大约五六年，他采取了更加温和妥协的路线。

sentences.en: So, for example, you don't have to be a communist in Hungary to hold a sort of senior administrative position.
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，在匈牙利，你不需要是共产党员就能担任某种高级行政职务。

sentences.en: And, Tom, great news for you.
sentences.zh: 托姆，这对你来说是个好消息。

sentences.en: In the first half, remember, I said because of your gentry background, all the massive handicaps under which your family would have to operate, no more.
sentences.zh: 还记得前半集我说过，由于你的士绅背景，你的家族将面临巨大的阻碍，这下不用担心了。

sentences.en: Under Kadar, your middle-class children can go to university.
sentences.zh: 在卡达尔统治下，你们中产阶级的孩子可以上大学了。

sentences.en: Oh, well, I'm rallying to Kadar then.
sentences.zh: 哦，那我可得支持卡达尔了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对啊。

sentences.en: I mean, just to say, I don't think I have a gentry background.
sentences.zh: 我是说，声明一下，我并不觉得自己有什么士绅背景。

sentences.en: I am, after all, of humble mining stock.
sentences.zh: 我毕竟出身于卑微的矿工家庭。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: But you're not a Marxist, are you?
sentences.zh: 但你又不是马克思主义者，对吧？

sentences.en: And Kadar would have wanted to appeal to you because he said in 1962, I want to appeal to hundreds of thousands of people who are not Marxists,
sentences.zh: 卡达尔本来也会想吸引你，因为他在1962年说过：我想吸引成百上千并非马克思主义者的人，

sentences.en: but who respect our party and our government for having created a legal order and a normal atmosphere in the country.
sentences.zh: 但他们尊重我们的党和政府，因为我们为这个国家创造了法治秩序和正常的氛围。

sentences.en: So is Hungary then the best place to be in the 60s, do you think?
sentences.zh: 那么，你觉得60年代的匈牙利是最好的生活地方吗？
是的，60年代、70年代、80年代。

sentences.en: Apart from Yugoslavia,
sentences.zh: 除了南斯拉夫，

sentences.en: Hungary is definitely the most liberal of the communist countries.
sentences.zh: 匈牙利绝对是共产主义国家中最自由的一个。

sentences.en: So Kadar's ethos, his slogan, his most famous saying, those who are not against us are with us.
sentences.zh: 所以卡达尔的精神内核、他的口号、他最著名的名言就是：不反对我们就是支持我们。

sentences.en: That's a great slogan, which is, you know, basically you don't have to be a communiSt.
sentences.zh: 这是个极棒的口号，你知道的，基本上就是你不需要当共产党员。

sentences.en: You don't have to like it.
sentences.zh: 你不需要喜欢它。

sentences.en: But as long as you don't do anything, it's fine and we'll look after you.
sentences.zh: 但只要你不搞事，那就没问题，我们会照顾你的。

sentences.en: And this is the ethos, Tom, of something called goulash communism.
sentences.zh: 托姆，这就是所谓的“古拉什共产主义”的精神内核。

sentences.en: Yeah, great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: So if you like goulash, you're laughing.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你喜欢古拉什牛肉汤，那你就有福了。

sentences.en: So basically what this involves, if you're Hungarian, you have to accept the communist party's monopoly of power and you have to accept the alliance of the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上这意味着，如果你是匈牙利人，你必须接受共产党对权力的垄断，你必须接受与苏联的同盟。

sentences.en: And if you just accept those two things, you know, the party is not going to repress you particularly or are not going to force you to live the sort of gray drab life
sentences.zh: 只要你接受这两点，你知道的，党就不会特别压迫你，也不会强迫你过那种你在别处可能会经历的灰暗沉闷的生活，

sentences.en: that you might get somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 那种你在别处可能会遭遇的生活。

sentences.en: So you can go to church.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以去教堂。

sentences.en: You can travel to the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 你可以去西方旅行。

sentences.en: You have a bit more freedom.
sentences.zh: 你拥有更多的自由。

sentences.en: There's a bit more free speech.
sentences.zh: 有更多的言论自由。

sentences.en: You have more washing machines than other people in the Warsaw Pact.
sentences.zh: 比起华沙条约集团的其他国家，你们拥有更多的洗衣机。

sentences.en: So it always comes back to washing machines.
sentences.zh: 所以最后总会绕回到洗衣机上。

sentences.en: So right up until the late 1980s, when this all fell apart,
sentences.zh: 因此，直到20世纪80年代末这一切土崩瓦解之前，

sentences.en: Hungary was known as the happiest barracks in Europe because of its more liberal regime.
sentences.zh: 由于其更自由的政体，匈牙利被称为欧洲最快乐的兵营。

sentences.en: So is this being a terrible story of failure and misery?
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个充满失败和苦难的糟糕故事吗？

sentences.en: Not necessarily.
sentences.zh: 未必如此。

sentences.en: So I mentioned Brian Cartlidge and his massive history of Hungary.
sentences.zh: 所以我提到了布赖恩·卡特利奇和他宏大的匈牙利历史著作。

sentences.en: His massive history of Hungary is called The Will to Survive.
sentences.zh: 他那部鸿篇巨制般的匈牙利史名为《生存的意志》。

sentences.en: And it's all about kind of Hungarian resilience.
sentences.zh: 书里讲的全是匈牙利人的韧性。

sentences.en: And he sees the revolution as a sort of landmark in that story.
sentences.zh: 他将这场革命视为这段历史中的一个里程碑。

sentences.en: It's actually something to be proud of rather than as a failure.
sentences.zh: 它实际上是一件值得骄傲的事，而不是一次失败。

sentences.en: I mean, it sounds like it was successful if you're getting your goulash.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，听上去只要有古拉什汤喝，那就挺成功的。

sentences.en: Well, it basically gives you – you've had a terrible time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，基本上它赋予了你——你们在20世纪前半叶经历了一段可怕的时期。

sentences.en: Hungary's had a terrible history in the first half of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 匈牙利在20世纪前半叶有着一段悲惨的历史。

sentences.en: You know, fascism, the Holocaust, occupation, all of this.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，法西斯主义、大屠杀、占领，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And this is something that even though it lost, it gives the Hungarians something to be proud of.
sentences.zh: 而这给匈牙利人提供了一种值得骄傲的东西，哪怕他们失败了。

sentences.en: They've been able to wave their national flag, sing their hymns.
sentences.zh: 他们能够挥舞国旗，高唱赞美诗。

sentences.en: They've rediscovered what Cartlidge calls their national self-respect.
sentences.zh: 他们重新找回了卡特利奇所说的“民族自尊”。

sentences.en: And actually, the big loser from all this is not Hungary.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这场动荡中最大的输家并不是匈牙利。

sentences.en: The big loser is Soviet communism.
sentences.zh: 最大的输家是苏联共产主义。

sentences.en: Because the Hungarian revolution, you know, you were saying, was it a turning point?
sentences.zh: 因为匈牙利革命，你刚才也说了，是一个转折点吗？

sentences.en: This deals an irreparable blow to the moral image of Soviet communism.
sentences.zh: 这给苏联共产主义的道德形象以沉重且无法弥补的打击。

sentences.en: So until even in the 1950s, there were people who said, you know, Stalin was an aberration.
sentences.zh: 所以在20世纪50年代甚至还有人说，斯大林只是个别现象。

sentences.en: Actually, you know, don't forget it was the Red Army who won the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 实际上，别忘了是红军赢得了第二次世界大战。

sentences.en: Or communism is still the best hope for a more equal, kinder future, all of this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 或者说共产主义仍然是建立一个更平等、更善良的未来的最佳希望，诸如此类的话。

sentences.en: But after 1956 and communist parties across Europe and indeed America,
sentences.zh: 但在1956年之后，欧洲乃至美国的共产党人、

sentences.en: intellectuals walk out and they say, I can't stomach this.
sentences.zh: 知识分子纷纷退党，他们说：我实在无法忍受了。

sentences.en: You know, the Soviet repression of the Hungarian revolution was the final straw.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，苏联对匈牙利革命的镇压成了压垮骆驼的最后一根稻草。

sentences.en: So people like E.P.
